shortcut_name: orbit connectivity reduces to weighted Steiner tree
evidence: The statement says "two variables belong to the same orbit if and only if one can be mapped to the other by some sequence of the selected operators"; the surviving solution builds an undirected graph with "adj[u].append((v, w))" and uses "full = 1 << t" subset DP.
affordance_in_statement: In the context of permutation groups, if we consider the subgroup of the symmetric group S_n generated by the selected transpositions, two variables belong to the same orbit if and only if one can be mapped to the other by some sequence of the selected operators.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving way to remove this affordance: for pairwise transpositions, subgroup orbits are intrinsically the connected components of the selected-edge graph, and allowing non-core variables intrinsically gives the Steiner-tree formulation. Only a genuine change of task, such as bounding operator composition or changing the operator type, would eliminate it.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the problem as the minimum weighted Steiner tree spanning the t core vertices and solves it with subset DP plus graph shortest-path transitions.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The selected transpositions generate orbits exactly equal to connected components, while non-core variables may be used as intermediate vertices.

common_affordance: The orbit condition is exactly weighted graph connectivity: selected transposition edges must connect all core vertices, with arbitrary non-core vertices allowed as Steiner vertices.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It computes shortest distances between core vertices and then treats the resulting metric closure as sufficient for the optimum, which misses sharing of non-core Steiner subtrees.

Its approach is described as "essentially" connecting the core variables with a minimum spanning-tree-style method, which is not sufficient for a general Steiner tree when non-core vertices can reduce cost.
It similarly models the task as an ordinary minimum spanning/connectivity problem rather than accounting for the exponentially many subsets of terminals and shared non-core Steiner structure.

recommended_edit: If the task must remain mathematically equivalent, no edit can defeat the surviving solution: this connectivity/Steiner reduction is the intrinsic structure. If changing the task is permitted, replace unrestricted subgroup composition by a bounded or ordered application rule for operators; that would invalidate the graph-connectivity reduction.
